headline: Ko, “child”, is cognate with 蚕 (ko, “silkworm”) and possibly 小 (ko, “little”).

sources.quote: ⟨ko₁⟩ → */kʷo/ → /ko/
From Old Japanese, attested in the Kojiki (712 CE) and the Man'yōshū (c. 759 CE), two of the oldest examples of written Japanese.
Cognate with 蚕 (ko, “silkworm”) and possibly 小 (ko, “little”, diminutive prefix).
Possibly cognate with Goguryeo 仇 (*gu), which appears in an ancient place name with an apparent meaning of child.

examples.ja: 親は子を愛する。
examples.en: Parents love their children.

examples.ja: 親の心子知らず。
examples.en: It is a wise father that knows his own child.

headline: Nokorazu is 残る (nokoru, “to remain”) plus ず (zu, negative continuative ending).

sources.quote: 残(のこ)る (nokoru, “to remain”) + ず (zu, negative continuative ending)

examples.ja: 秘密を残らず打ち明けなさい。
examples.en: Make a clean breast of your secrets.

examples.ja: 彼は有り金を残らず奪われた。
examples.en: He was robbed of all his money.

headline: Jikanwari is 時間 (jikan) plus 割 (wari).

sources.quote: 時(じ)間(かん) (jikan) + 割(わり) (wari)

examples.ja: 時間割をもらえますか。
examples.en: May I have a class schedule?

examples.ja: 私たちは時間割に従って勉強する。
examples.en: We study according to the schedule.

headline: Yobidasu is yobi, the stem of 呼ぶ (yobu, “to call”), plus 出す (-dasu, “out”).

sources.quote: 呼(よ)び (yobi, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 呼(よ)ぶ (yobu, “to call”)) + 出(だ)す (-dasu, “out”)

examples.ja: 彼は私を呼びだした。
examples.en: He called me out.

examples.ja: 彼を電話口に呼び出した。
examples.en: I called him to the telephone.

meaning: to be in high spirits, to be full of vigor
headline: Harikiru is 張る (haru, “be enthusiastic”) plus 切る (kiru, “perform an action decisively”).

sources.quote: From 張る (haru, "be enthusiastic") + 切る (kiru, "perform an action decisively").

headline: Shitsukoi has no certain origin: the second element could be 濃い (koi, “thick”), and the first is uncertain.

sources.quote: The second element could be 濃(こ)い (koi, “thick”), and the first element remains uncertain. It could be 為付(しつ)ける (shitsukeru, “to accustom”), but is semantically problematic.

Another theory regards it as a deverbal adjective of 執(しっ)する (shissuru, “to insist”) and thinks that it was contaminated by 懐(なつ)こい (natsukoi, “easy to become acquainted with anyone”) and 熱濃(ねつこ)い (netsukoi, “enthusiastic; persistent”), but the earlier meaning of this word is "very rich and thick", so this theory is also historical semantically problematic.
Morphologically, just like 懐(なつ)く (natsuku) and 懐(なつ)こい (natsukoi), 執拗(しつこ)い (shitsukoi)
could be also derived from 為付(しつ)く (shitsuku, “to become practised”), but is still problematic on meaning.

headline: Mētoru is from French mètre, a doublet of メーター (mētā).

sources.quote: From French mètre. Doublet of メーター (mētā, “meter”, measuring instrument).

examples.ja: 前の人から1メートル離れて並んでください。
examples.en: Form a line, keeping one meter away from the person in front of you.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Urikire is the nominalization of the verb 売り切れる (urikireru).

sources.quote: From the nominalization of the verb 売(う)り切(き)れる (urikireru).

examples.ja: みんな売り切れです。
examples.en: All sold out!

examples.ja: 切符はすべて売り切れです。
examples.en: All the tickets are sold out.

headline: Sūgaku is 数 (sū, “number”) plus 学 (-gaku, “-logy; -graphy”).

sources.quote: From 数(すう) (sū, “number”) + 学(がく) (-gaku, “-logy; -graphy”).

examples.ja: 数学が得意です。
examples.en: I am good at math.

examples.ja: 私は数学が弱い。
examples.en: I am weak in mathematics.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Bakuhatsu is Middle Chinese 爆發, literally “burst, explode + fly or send forth”.

sources.quote: /pakupatu/ → /bakufat͡su/ → /bakuhat͡su/
From Middle Chinese compound 爆發 /爆发 (pɑk pjot, literally “burst, explode + fly or send forth”). Compare modern Min Nan reading po̍k-hoat.

examples.ja: 突然爆発が起こった。
examples.en: All at once there was an explosion.

examples.ja: 彼は怒りを爆発させた。
examples.en: He exploded with anger.

headline: Tanomoshii is from the Early Middle Japanese adjective 頼もし (tanomoshi), whose ending later lost its medial k.

sources.quote: From Early Middle Japanese adjective 頼(たの)もし (tanomoshi), with the 終(しゅう)止(し)形(けい) (shūshikei, “predicative form”) ending in し (shi) first replaced with the 連(れん)体(たい)形(けい) (rentaikei, “attributive form”) ending in しき (shiki), and then with the medial /-k-/ falling out to result in an ending of しい (shii). Itself an adjectivization of the verb 頼(たの)む (tanomu, “to request; to entrust to”).

examples.ja: 彼は頼もしい男だ。
examples.en: He is a man to be depended on.

headline: Uwa is the combining form of ue, ancient upe.

sources.quote: /upa/ → /ufa/ → /uwa/
From Old Japanese. The combining form of ue, ancient upe (see above).

headline: Keikōtō is 蛍光 (keikō, “fluorescent”) plus 灯 (tō, “light”).

sources.quote: Compound of 蛍(けい)光(こう) (keikō, “fluorescent”) + 灯(とう) (tō, “light”).

examples.ja: ハリーは本当に蛍光灯だね。

examples.ja: そこの蛍光灯を交換しないといけない。

headline: Gikai is 議 (“debate; deliberation; discussion”) plus 会 (“gathering”).

sources.quote: 議 (“debate; deliberation; discussion”) + 会 (“gathering”)

examples.ja: 議会は解散した。

examples.ja: 議会は休会になりました。

headline: Sōzō is Middle Chinese 創造, literally “to begin + to make”.

sources.quote: /sauzau/ → /sɔːzɔː/ → /soːzoː/
From Middle Chinese compound 創造 /创造 (t͡ʃʰɨɐŋᴴ d͡zɑu^X, literally “to begin + to make”). Compare modern Mandarin reading chuàngzào, Cantonese cong³ zou⁶.

examples.ja: 神は宇宙を創造した。

examples.ja: 神が世界を創造した。

headline: Tōge, a mountain pass, is a sound shift from 手向け (tamuke, “tribute to a person about to depart”).

sources.quote: /tamuke/ → /taũɡe/ → /tauɡe/ → /tɔːɡe/ → /toːɡe/
Sound shift from 手向け (tamuke, “tribute to a person about to depart”). It is said that these offerings were "given" to them as they traveled into the afterlife, akin to a mountain.

examples.ja: 私達が峠にさしかかる頃に雨になった。
examples.en: It began to rain as we came near the pass.

headline: Fukisoku is 不 (fu-, “un-; non-”) plus 規則 (kisoku, “rule”).

sources.quote: Compound of 不(ふ) (fu-, “un-; non-”) + 規(き)則(そく) (kisoku, “rule”).

examples.ja: 生理が不規則です。

examples.ja: 彼は出席が不規則だ。

headline: Yuki, “bound for”, is compared on its page to Korean 행 (haeng), written with the same 行.

sources.quote: Compare Korean 행(行) (haeng).

meaning: telephone pole, telegraph pole, light pole
headline: Denchū is 電 (den, “electric”) plus 柱 (chū, “pole”).

sources.quote: 電 (den, “electric”) + 柱 (chū, “pole”)

examples.ja: 技師が電柱を上った。

examples.ja: 車は電柱にぶつかった。

sources.quote: 総理 (“prime minister”, literally “leader”) + 大臣 (“(senior) minister”)

headline: Tetsudō is 鉄 (tetsu, “iron, steel”) plus 道 (dō, “way”), a calque of German Eisenbahn.

sources.quote: 鉄(てつ) (tetsu, “iron, steel”) + 道(どう) (dō, “way”). Calque of German Eisenbahn.

sources.quote: Note similarities to Proto-Tai *tacᴰ (“to cut”) (whence Thai ตัด (dtàt, “to cut”)).

examples.ja: 彼女はきっぱり断った。

examples.ja: 彼らは食料の供給を断たれた。
examples.en: They were cut off from food supplies.

headline: Nokori is the continuative stem of 残る (nokoru, “to remain”).

sources.quote: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 残(のこ)る (nokoru, “to remain”).

examples.en: Keep the rest for yourself.

headline: Makkura is 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) plus 暗 (kura, “dark”).

sources.quote: 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) + 暗 (kura, “dark”)

examples.ja: 空は真っ暗だった。
examples.en: The sky was completely dark.

examples.ja: 外は真っ暗だった。
examples.en: It was pitch black outside.

headline: Nanika is 何 (nani, “what”) plus か (ka, indefinite particle).

sources.quote: From 何(なに) (nani, “what”) + か (ka, indefinite particle).

examples.ja: なにか問題でも？
examples.en: What's the matter?

examples.ja: なにか飲み物でも？
examples.en: Would you care for something to drink?

headline: Umai is from the Early Middle Japanese adjective うまし (umashi), its ending reshaped in two steps.

sources.quote: From Early Middle Japanese adjective うまし (umashi), with the 終(しゅう)止(し)形(けい) (shūshikei, “predicative form”) ending in し (shi) first replaced with the 連(れん)体(たい)形(けい) (rentaikei, “attributive form”) ending in き (ki), and then with the medial /-k-/ falling out to result in an ending of い (i). From Old Japanese. Found in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE. Sometimes reconstructed as Proto-Japonic *uma.

The ultimate derivation remains unclear. The term occasionally appears in texts from the Heian period (794–1185 CE) with the phonetic spelling mumashi (in the classical terminal form), suggesting a possible pronunciation of */mmasi/ with an emphasized initial /mm/ sound, similar to the reconstructed readings for 馬 (*mma, “horse”) and 梅 (*mme, “plum”). The resulting reconstructed adjective stem of *mma- could indicate a derivation from onomatopoeia; compare English mmm as an expression of approval for something tasty.

Alternatively, umai is listed in some sources as perhaps deriving from verb 熟む (umu, “to ripen, to become ripe”). There is a derived compound term where the meaning is clearly from the adjective, and the spelling uses the 熟 kanji from the verb. However, the verb does not appear in historical sources with an emphatic initial /mm/, and it seems to be cognate with 膿む (umu, “to fester, to fill with pus, to produce pus”, intransitive), possibly also with 生む, 産む (umu, “to bear, to give birth to; to produce”, transitive).
Reconstructed by Samuel Martin as Proto-Japonic *ma-. Compare Okinawan cognate まーさん (māsan).

headline: Waku is a kokuji, a Japanese-coined character: 木 plus 卆, and not a simplification of 木 plus 卒.

sources.quote: A 国字 (kokuji, “Japanese-coined character”). 木 + 卆; it is not a simplification of 木 + 卒 (椊).

examples.ja: 彼はドア枠の下に立った。
examples.en: He stood under the door frame.

examples.ja: 民主党は選挙運動のために民放テレビの放送枠を買いました。
examples.en: The Democrats bought space on commercial television for the campaign.

headline: Mendōkusai is 面倒 (“inconvenience”) plus 臭い (“reeks of”).

sources.quote: 面倒 (“inconvenience”) + 臭い (“reeks of”)

examples.ja: そこまで歩いて行くのはめんどうくさい。
examples.en: It's too much trouble to walk there.

meaning: (col) round trip, coming and going, return ticket

nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Ōfuku, “round trip”, began as waupuku and lost its w along the way.

sources.quote: /waupukʉ/ → /wɔːɸuku/ → /ɔːfuku/ → /oːfuku/

examples.ja: 往復びんたを食らった。
examples.en: I got slapped on both cheeks.

examples.ja: 往復ですか、片道ですか。
examples.en: Round trip or one-way?

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: In kaiten, 回 is a daiyōji replacing 廻.

sources.quote: 回 is a daiyōji replacing 廻.

examples.ja: 姉は頭の回転がいい。
examples.en: My sister is quick-thinking.

examples.ja: 車輪は車軸で回転する。
examples.en: Wheels turn on axles.
